application.product: Cypress Real World App — a peer-to-peer payment application
application.frontend: create-react-app 4 single-page application (TypeScript) with XState state machines
application.backend: first-party, in this repository: an Express server under backend/ over a lowdb JSON document, with REST routes, a GraphQL endpoint, passport authentication and express-validator validation. It is a real application server, not a test harness stub.
application.persistence: lowdb 1.0.0 over data/database.json, seeded from data/database-seed.json
application.apiSurface: REST: /users /contacts /bankAccounts /transactions /likes /comments /notifications /bankTransfers, plus /login /logout /checkAuth and a /testData route mounted only in development and test. GraphQL at /graphql with graphiql enabled.

authMode.howSelected: By the absence of every provider variable. src/index.tsx branches on REACT_APP_AUTH0, REACT_APP_OKTA, REACT_APP_AWS_COGNITO and REACT_APP_GOOGLE in that order and falls through to a final else that renders src/containers/App.tsx. backend/app.ts always mounts backend/auth.ts and mounts the matching JWT middleware only when the same variable is set. The committed .env leaves all four commented out, so `yarn dev` and `yarn start` are already local mode with no flags.
authMode.mechanism: passport-local plus express-session, NOT JWT. POST /login compares the submitted password against the bcrypt hash in the lowdb seed and returns a connect.sid session cookie. The JWT libraries in the closure (express-jwt, jwks-rsa, @okta/jwt-verifier) serve only the four external-provider modes.
authMode.correctionNote: The T007 scout described this as a 'local JWT mode'. The offline conclusion is correct; the JWT description is not. Recorded so no later unit looks for a token that local mode never issues.
authMode.demonstrated: POST /login returned 200 against the booted in-repo API with zero external hosts contacted.

knownRisks: Holdout discipline: nothing learned from this fixture may be used to change the frozen adapters. Findings below are findings, not work items.

Vendor-authored cleanliness. This is a Cypress-maintained showcase that installs, typechecks and builds cleanly with zero deviations. As a falsification target it is a well-formed CRA 4 application rather than a decayed one, so a pass here is weaker evidence than a pass on a decayed application, and a failure would be correspondingly stronger.

Four external identity providers (Auth0, Okta, AWS Cognito/Amplify, Google) are wired in src/index.tsx and backend/app.ts and remain in the dependency closure — and therefore in the production bundle — even though local mode never activates them. Any later browser work must leave REACT_APP_AUTH0, REACT_APP_OKTA, REACT_APP_AWS_COGNITO and REACT_APP_GOOGLE unset.

backend/helpers.ts requires ../src/aws-exports unconditionally, and that file is git-ignored and absent from the pinned revision. A clean checkout cannot boot the API until the repository's own copy:mock:awsexports script has run. This is a first-boot obstacle for any unit that starts the server.

data/database.json is both committed and the live lowdb store the API writes to. Any journey that writes will dirty the tree; restore it from data/database-seed.json rather than treating it as immutable.

The dev server runs through @cypress/instrument-cra, which injects istanbul instrumentation. The dev-server path and the production-build path therefore differ, and only the production build was exercised here.

data/database-seed.json holds faker-generated person-shaped records and bcrypt hashes. It is synthetic fixture data, not personal data; no seed value is reproduced in any Versionless evidence file and none may be introduced by later work.
Honouring the repository's Node 14.16.1 pin requires Rosetta 2 on Apple Silicon, since Node 14 has no darwin-arm64 build.
